title: Standard-cell layout
subject: One gate, one clear view.
guide: Add a clear, shareable screenshot of your inverter, logic gate, or adder layout. Crop tightly enough to see the layers.
tip: Use a direct screenshot instead of photographing your screen.

title: Analog layout overview
subject: Show the overall organization.
guide: Use an approved overview of a bandgap, op-amp, or LDO layout. A conceptual floorplan also works when the actual layout cannot be shared.
tip: Remove confidential names and use only images you are allowed to show.

title: SKILL automation
subject: Show the before and after.
guide: Place two screenshots side by side to show what your script changes: labels, metal layers, bindkeys, or a repeated layout task.
tip: Use the same zoom and crop in both screenshots. Keep text readable.

title: You at your workstation
subject: Show the person behind the work.
guide: Use a landscape photo of you working at a tidy engineering desk. An over-the-shoulder angle works well.
tip: Keep the monitor content shareable and leave space around the subject.

title: Your robot or vehicle
subject: Keep the whole platform in view.
guide: Photograph your UAV, UGV, USV, or ROV from a three-quarter angle. Include the full vehicle and a little of its working environment.
tip: Use one project per cover image. Keep the background uncluttered.

title: Hardware integration
subject: Get closer to your contribution.
guide: Add a well-lit close-up of a flight controller, Raspberry Pi, sensor, or wiring arrangement you integrated.
tip: Show the component and enough surrounding hardware to explain where it sits.

title: Your professional portrait
subject: A simple, natural introduction.
guide: Use a head-and-shoulders photo in a plain shirt, against a clean light background. Look toward the camera with a relaxed expression.
tip: Leave space above your head. A phone photo in soft window light is suitable.

title: Teamwork or demonstration
subject: Show an activity, not only a pose.
guide: Add a photo of you discussing a project, demonstrating hardware, or helping in a workshop.
tip: Choose an image where your role is clear and the people pictured are comfortable being shown.

title: Your earned digital badge
subject: Use the original badge artwork.
guide: Upload the original PNG or SVG from the issuer and include its verification link. Keep the entire badge visible.
tip: This sample is an example format, not an earned credential.

title: Your certificate or training record
subject: Keep the full document readable.
guide: Use a clear PDF, scan, or straight-on photo showing all four edges. Include the course title, issuer, and date as separate text.
tip: Preserve the document proportions. Cover private IDs if needed.
